Measures what your connection really exposes, item by item. It only runs when you tap Start, so it never costs battery in the background.

Why
How to fix
How it\'s measured
Measured
Your traffic leaves through the Tor network
Sites see a Tor exit, not your server. Many sites block or slow Tor, and the exit operator can see unencrypted traffic.
Traffic leaves via the server
Sites see the server\'s address, not yours.
No exit address came back, or it is in your own country.
Pick another server, or reconnect.
Asks ip.sb / ip-api.com through the tunnel, and once without it, and compares the countries.
Connection is encrypted
This config uses TLS, REALITY or an encrypted protocol.
Without TLS or REALITY the traffic is easy to spot and read.
Use a config with TLS or REALITY.
Reads the selected config\'s protocol and security settings.
Server certificate is checked
The server\'s certificate is verified, so nobody can impersonate it.
“Allow insecure” is on: anyone in the middle could pose as the server.
Edit the config and turn off Allow insecure, or pin the certificate.
Reads allowInsecure and certificate pinning from the selected config.
Looks like a normal browser
The TLS handshake mimics a common browser.
An unusual TLS fingerprint makes the connection easier to single out.
Set the fingerprint to chrome in the config.
Reads the uTLS fingerprint of the selected config (blank means chrome).
No one is intercepting HTTPS
A real HTTPS site answered with a valid certificate over TLS 1.3.
The certificate failed to verify, or TLS was downgraded: something may be intercepting.
Switch server, and remove unknown certificates from Settings › Security.
Opens cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/trace through the tunnel with full certificate checks and reads the TLS version.
Tunnel responds quickly
A round trip through the tunnel was quick.
The tunnel is slow or not answering.
Try another server, or Game mode for lower delay.
Times one HTTPS request to cp.cloudflare.com/generate_204 through the tunnel (under 900 ms passes).
DNS doesn\'t leak
Website lookups are answered outside your country.
Lookups are answered inside your country: your provider can see which sites you open.
Turn on Secure mode, or set Remote DNS to https://1.1.1.1/dns-query.
Resolves a random name under edns.ip-api.com through the tunnel and reads which resolver asked.
DNS sits with the exit
The resolver is in the same country as the exit.
The resolver is in another country than the exit: harmless, but sites may notice.
Use a DoH resolver near your server.
Compares the resolver\'s country with the exit country.
DNS is encrypted
Remote DNS uses DNS-over-HTTPS or TLS.
Remote DNS is plain: it rides the tunnel, but the server\'s network can read it.
Set Remote DNS to https://1.1.1.1/dns-query, or use Secure mode.
Reads the Remote DNS setting (the active mode included).
IPv6 can\'t slip out
The VPN claims all IPv6 routes, so IPv6 goes through the tunnel or nowhere.
In proxy-only mode other apps can use IPv6 directly.
Use VPN mode in Settings.
Checks VPN mode (::/0 is routed into the tunnel) and asks api6.ipify.org through it.
WebRTC / UDP stays inside
All UDP, including WebRTC, enters the tunnel, so calls can\'t reveal your address.
In proxy-only mode WebRTC in other apps can reveal your real address.
Use VPN mode in Settings.
Checks whether the full-route VPN is used (it carries every UDP packet).
Proxy is private to this phone
The local proxy only listens on this phone.
The proxy is shared on your Wi-Fi; others there can use it.
Turn off LAN sharing, or set a username and password.
Reads the LAN-sharing and proxy authentication settings.
Kill switch
Always-on VPN with blocking is on: nothing leaks if the tunnel drops.
If the tunnel drops, apps fall back to your normal connection for a moment.
Android Settings › VPN › SatraNG › Always-on and Block connections without VPN.
Reported by Android when the tunnel starts (isAlwaysOn / isLockdownEnabled). Optional, so not scored.
Screen lock is set
A PIN, pattern or password protects this phone.
Anyone holding the phone can open your apps and configs.
Settings › Security › Screen lock.
KeyguardManager.isDeviceSecure.
USB debugging is off
No computer can control this phone over USB debugging.
USB debugging is on: a paired computer can read app data.
Developer options › turn off USB / wireless debugging when you don\'t need it.
Reads Settings.Global.ADB_ENABLED.
Security updates are recent
The Android security patch is less than four months old.
The security patch is old; known holes may be open.
Settings › System update.
Compares Build.VERSION.SECURITY_PATCH with today.
No extra certificates trusted
Only Android\'s built-in certificate authorities are trusted.
A user-installed certificate can let someone read HTTPS in some apps.
Settings › Security › Encryption & credentials › User credentials: remove ones you don\'t know.
Counts user: entries in the AndroidCAStore key store.
Android Private DNS
Private DNS is on for your normal connection.
Private DNS is off; the tunnel handles DNS while connected.
Optional: Settings › Network › Private DNS.
LinkProperties.isPrivateDnsActive. Information only.
Tor Project\'s own check
check.torproject.org says this is not a Tor exit.
check.torproject.org says your traffic comes from Tor.
If you didn\'t expect Tor, choose another server.
Asks check.torproject.org/api/ip through the tunnel.
Exit list lookup
Your exit address is not in the Tor exit list.
Your exit address is a known Tor exit.
If you didn\'t expect Tor, choose another server.
Looks the exit up in the Tor bulk exit list, saved on the phone so it also works offline.
Relay directory
The exit address is not a Tor relay.
The exit address runs a Tor relay.
Nothing to do unless you didn\'t expect Tor.
Searches onionoo.torproject.org for the exit address, through the tunnel.
Offline Tor list
The saved Tor exit list is fresh.
The saved list is old; it refreshes on the next check when online.
Run the check again while connected.
Age of the list saved from check.torproject.org/torbulkexitlist (refreshed daily, only during a check, via the tunnel).
